import pandas as pd
from pandas.api.types import is_datetime64_any_dtype

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    dim_product = inputs["dim_product"].copy()
    stg_product = inputs["stg_product"].copy()
    
    # Ensure datetime columns are in consistent nanosecond precision for comparison
    if len(dim_product) > 0:
        dim_product["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_product["eff_start_date"])
        dim_product["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_product["eff_end_date"])
    
    if len(stg_product) > 0:
        stg_product["update_date"] = pd.to_datetime(stg_product["update_date"])
    
    # Sort staged records by product_id, then update_date (ascending)
    stg_sorted = stg_product.sort_values(by=["product_id", "update_date"], na_position="last").reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Process each staged record in order
    for idx, s_row in stg_sorted.iterrows():
        s_product_id = s_row["product_id"]
        s_category = s_row["category"]
        s_price_band = s_row["price_band"]
        s_update_date = s_row["update_date"]
        
        # Find current row for this product_id
        current_rows = dim_product[(dim_product["product_id"] == s_product_id) & (dim_product["is_current"] == 1)]
        
        if len(current_rows) == 0:
            # Insert new current version
            new_row = {
                "product_id": s_product_id,
                "category": s_category,
                "price_band": s_price_band,
                "eff_start_date": s_update_date,
                "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                "is_current": 1
            }
            dim_product = pd.concat([dim_product, pd.DataFrame([new_row])], ignore_index=True)
        else:
            # Get the current row (should be only one)
            c_row = current_rows.iloc[0]
            c_category = c_row["category"]
            c_price_band = c_row["price_band"]
            
            # Check if category or price_band changed (NULL handling: NULL != non-NULL, NULL == NULL)
            category_changed = False
            if pd.isna(c_category) and pd.isna(s_category):
                category_changed = False
            elif pd.isna(c_category) or pd.isna(s_category):
                category_changed = True
            elif c_category != s_category:
                category_changed = True
            
            price_band_changed = False
            if pd.isna(c_price_band) and pd.isna(s_price_band):
                price_band_changed = False
            elif pd.isna(c_price_band) or pd.isna(s_price_band):
                price_band_changed = True
            elif c_price_band != s_price_band:
                price_band_changed = True
            
            if category_changed or price_band_changed:
                # Expire current row
                current_idx = dim_product[(dim_product["product_id"] == s_product_id) & (dim_product["is_current"] == 1)].index[0]
                dim_product.loc[current_idx, "eff_end_date"] = s_update_date
                dim_product.loc[current_idx, "is_current"] = 0
                
                # Insert new current version
                new_row = {
                    "product_id": s_product_id,
                    "category": s_category,
                    "price_band": s_price_band,
                    "eff_start_date": s_update_date,
                    "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                    "is_current": 1
                }
                dim_product = pd.concat([dim_product, pd.DataFrame([new_row])], ignore_index=True)
            # else: no-op, unchanged record does not create a version
    
    dim_product = dim_product.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"dim_product_out": dim_product}
